metadata.title: Start a chapter in Eindhoven, Delft or The Hague
metadata.description: SAIN is starting chapters in Eindhoven, Delft and The Hague. Each city gets a paid, part-time starting team of four: a Chapter Director and leads for education, events and communications.

hero.heading: Start SAIN in Eindhoven, Delft or The Hague.
hero.intro: SAIN has chapters in Groningen, Amsterdam and Utrecht. This winter we are starting three more: Eindhoven, Delft and The Hague. Each city gets a starting team of four people: a Chapter Director, an Education Lead, an Events Lead and a Communications Lead. All four roles are paid and part-time.
hero.deadline: Soft deadline {date}. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, with priority to early applicants.

map.title: SAIN’s chapters in the Netherlands
map.description: Chapters run in Groningen, Amsterdam and Utrecht. Starting teams are wanted in Eindhoven, Delft and The Hague.

building.heading: You would be building a chapter, not joining one.
building.body: You would be the person building a SAIN chapter in your city, and you will be in charge of setting up everything. However, you’ll have support: a funded national organisation behind you, and a network of advisors, researchers and partner organisations who want nothing more than your chapter to succeed.

cities.heading: Three cities with the most potential.
cities.intro: We have identified these three cities as the highest-potential ones for us to expand to. Here is, very briefly, why we think so.

eindhoven.origin: TU/e, the Center for Safe AI and the Brainport region
eindhoven.why: Brainport is home to ASML and one of Europe's densest clusters of engineering talent.
eindhoven.profile: Likely a valuable technical chapter with some important governance questions sprinkled in: interpretability, evaluations, engineering, compute verification and the governance of the hardware AI runs on.

delft.why: The largest technical university in the Netherlands, with deep strengths in robotics and embodied AI. TU Delft's ELLIS unit coordinates themes including Verification & Safe and Responsible AI, Multiagent Systems & Robust and Adversarial ML, and Sequential Decision Making.
delft.profile: Likely also a strong technical chapter, with a potentially stronger emphasis on embodied AI safety.

the-hague.why: Ministries, regulators, international institutions, and Leiden University's Campus The Hague and the Haagse Hogeschool. Notably strong for cybersecurity, with national and international cyber institutions, including The Hague Security Delta (HSD), a major European security cluster.
the-hague.profile: Likely a strong governance chapter that reaches civil servants and policy professionals as much as students.

cities.inTouch: We are already in touch with people working on AI safety in these cities. Where people have already been running things, we can build on top of that and be much more ambitious. Already running something there and not heard from us yet? <link>Please get in touch</link>, so we can work together instead of duplicating efforts.

incubation.heading: Six months from starting team to SAIN chapter.
paragraphs: New chapters start as incubating chapters. From mid-December 2026 to June 2027, the starting team will develop the chapter towards a few concrete milestones. Importantly, although this phase is part of the incubation, internally we’ll treat you as a SAIN chapter from the start.

We’re ambitious about this. In some of these cities, people already run AI safety courses, and we want to build on that and go much further: courses with dozens of participants, events that bring hundreds of new people into AI safety, a community of hundreds in every city, and people moving on into real projects.

The exact milestones for June 2027 we’ll set together with you in your first weeks; how you get there is up to you. We’ll work together to make sure you reach your fullest potential. In June 2027 we will do a final review of how things have gone. Chapters that get there become official SAIN chapters, and the director and lead roles stay paid part-time positions.

community.heading: This is what you would be starting.
community.body: Discussion groups, hackathons, talks, and the evenings after. In Groningen, Amsterdam and Utrecht, people meet friends and collaborators at SAIN, and often find their next step in AI safety. Apply now, and a year from now your city has a community like this, built by you.

offer.heading: You won’t be doing it alone.
offer.intro: Everything the three existing chapters learned the hard way is written down, set up, and yours from day one.

director.title: Chapter Director
director.summary: Leads the starting team and opens the city's doors.
director.hours: 12 hours a week depending on preference and availability, {term}.
about: Every SAIN chapter started with one person who had a vision and made it happen. In Groningen, Amsterdam and Utrecht that took years of trial and error. In Eindhoven, Delft and The Hague we want it to take six months, because this time the director has all of SAIN's resources to get started.

As the Director, you would be the person leading everything in your city. You will develop the team (and will even be included in the final interviews of the other starting team roles in your city if possible) and open the doors to collaboration: at the university or hogescholen, with local organisations, and in The Hague with the ministries and institutions. By June there should be a chapter that runs basically autonomously. You work directly with SAIN's national team, and you are accountable for whether your city reaches its milestones.

Importantly: this role is about building, and about people. Whilst AI safety knowledge is helpful, your job is to gather the most knowledgeable people into your community, not to be that person yourself. You need enough grounding to represent the field credibly, which is why we ask, at least, for a completed AI safety course. You are the one that builds, that keeps the team together, and that multiplies what everyone else does.

This means we expect high agency from you. For instance, you will not get a week-by-week checklist. Instead, we will set the destination together, you then choose the route, and you pull in support when you need it.

What the chapter looks like depends on the city. In Eindhoven and Delft, a technical profile fits best: you will mostly be talking to engineers, students and researchers. In The Hague, the director is ideally someone who knows how the government works from the inside. It is your job to identify your city's strengths and steer AI safety into the field.
firstMonths: Grow your starting team to at least four people with clear roles, starting with the leads selected alongside you. We will help by sharing other applicants with you.

Secure office space and use your connections within the city for collaborations and useful advisors that can help you navigate the city and develop the chapter. We will help with budget and connections.
Get the chapter's communications going and schedule your first course for spring.
responsibilities: Lead the starting team: set direction, run the weekly team meeting, clear blockers, and bring in new members as the chapter grows.

Build the chapter's relationships with the university and local organisations, and set priorities accordingly. For example, in The Hague, relationships with the government and international institutions are most important.
Own the chapter's plan, milestones and budget, together with the national team.
Represent the chapter at events, with partners and in the press.
Write a short monthly update for the national team: what happened, the numbers, blockers, and next month's plans.
Bring your city's perspective and opportunities into SAIN's national decisions.
goodFitIf: Have built something from scratch, or led a team, community, project or initiative, and can tell us what went wrong and what you did about it.
Have completed an AI safety course (BlueDot, ARENA, a SAIN course or similar), or have equivalent knowledge of the field.
Have a track record of chasing things to a finished state without being asked. Being proactive matters a lot!
Are comfortable with ambiguity, with delegating, and with speaking in front of a room.
Live in or near the city and will be there until at least June 2027.
alsoStrong: Experience in an AI safety organisation.
A network in the city: at the university, in local industry, or in government.
For The Hague: experience inside government, a regulator or an international institution.
Professional working proficiency in Dutch (especially valuable in The Hague).

logistics.compensation: €42–50k a year at full-time (40 hours), pro-rated to your hours.
logistics.reportsTo: Your mentor on SAIN's national team.

education-lead.title: Education Lead
education-lead.summary: Brings the first AI safety course to the city.
education-lead.hours: 8 hours a week depending on preference and availability, {term}.
about: Courses are where most people's path into AI safety begins. At SAIN, hundreds of people a year take one at our existing chapters, and many of them go on to (research) projects, jobs and chapter roles of their own. In your city, SAIN's first course does not exist yet. You make it exist!

You will not have to write a curriculum. We already have a clear playbook and curricula running in three cities, with readings, session plans and facilitator guides. Your job is to bring one to your city, get as many of the best people in your city to join, make sure they finish, and go on to develop themselves further.
Which course comes first depends on the city: most likely a technical track in Eindhoven and Delft, and a governance & policy track in The Hague. You decide this with your director.
firstMonths: Choose the first course and track with your director, and schedule it for spring.
Find the right place for people to do the course, recruit and onboard the appropriate number of facilitators, and get ready for applications! We will help you set up the application process.
Promote the first cohort with your Communications Lead.
By June: dozens of people through your courses, aiming for more than a hundred across the spring, and documented lessons to run them even better next year.
responsibilities: Plan and run course iterations using SAIN's curricula and the Education Handbook.
Start and run discussion groups.
Recruit, train and support facilitators and discussion leads, with help from SAIN.
Run course logistics: design each cohort, book rooms, process applications, plan and execute the project phase, and celebrate all participants in a graduation ceremony!
Coordinate with the Communications Lead on marketing, and with the Events Lead on course-related events.
Attend to the chapter's education inbox, and escalate matters to your Director or SAIN's national team where appropriate.
goodFitIf: Are organised, write clearly, and enjoy getting a group to think together. The role requires good administrative attention.
Have completed an AI safety course.
Are comfortable with both technical and governance content. You do not need to be an expert in either.
alsoStrong: A master's degree (finished or in progress), or professional experience in education.
Connections to study associations or teaching staff at TU/e, TU Delft, Leiden University The Hague or the Haagse Hogeschool (whichever is appropriate to your city).
Experience facilitating an AI safety course.

logistics.compensation: €34–42k a year at full-time (40 hours), pro-rated to your hours.

events-lead.title: Events Lead
events-lead.summary: Makes the chapter visible, one event at a time.
events-lead.hours: 8 hours a week depending on preference and availability, {term}.
about: Events are how a chapter becomes visible. A good talk or hackathon is where most people first meet the community. It is also where the people who will later run its courses and projects first show up. In a new city, every event is also proof that there are people here who take AI safety seriously.

You plan and run the chapter's first events, from the first meetup to talks that people travel for. You do not start from zero: SAIN's events playbook, speakers from the other chapters' networks, and a budget are there. What we need is someone who makes events happen reliably, gets the right people in the room, and makes them want to come back. That will be you!

The audience differs per city. In Eindhoven it is TU/e students and Brainport engineers, and in Delft TU Delft students and researchers. In The Hague it is civil servants, policy professionals and students. Your role is to deliver events that build on your city's strengths and opportunities. Each event is an opportunity to bring the local community and newcomers together while representing SAIN's mission and values authentically.
firstMonths: Run the chapter's first public event early in the new year.
Build a spring calendar with a mix of talks, socials and at least one hands-on format, such as a hackathon or reading group.
Find two or three venues you can rely on, and start a list of local speakers.
By June: regular events that have brought hundreds of new faces to AI safety in your city, each with a clear next step for the people who came.
responsibilities: Plan a balanced calendar of professional events, community socials and hackathons using SAIN's Events Handbook, and share key dates with the Communications Lead early.
Recruit and brief speakers, both locally and through SAIN's network.
Run event logistics: booking venues, selecting and ordering catering, enabling sign-ups, and the handover to Communications to promote every event.
Spot opportunities for the chapter and SAIN to appear at other people's events.
Attend to the chapter's events inbox, and escalate matters to your Director or SAIN's national team where appropriate.
goodFitIf: Have organised events before, for example for a study association, conference, hackathon, festival or company.
Are comfortable cold-emailing speakers and venues, and following up until you get an answer.
Stay calm when something goes wrong an hour before the doors open.
Have a genuine interest in AI safety. No real background is required, though we expect you to upskill rapidly.
alsoStrong: A network in the city's student, tech or policy scene.
Experience with hackathons or professional events.
Experience with Luma or similar event tools.

logistics.compensation: €34–42k a year at full-time (40 hours), pro-rated to your hours.

communications-lead.title: Communications Lead
communications-lead.summary: Builds the chapter's audience in the city.
communications-lead.hours: 8 hours a week depending on preference and availability, {term}.
about: Nobody joins something they have never heard of. That is where you come in! You make sure the right people in your city hear about AI safety: researchers and professionals who would make great facilitators, engineers and students who have been quietly worried about the progress of AI and need a community, and civil servants who want to understand what is actually going on.

You launch the chapter's social media accounts and make them run reliably. As SAIN, we have a brand kit, templates and more that are ready to be used. You will be working together with the national team and the other chapters' Communications Leads to share what works and what doesn't. Building the chapter's audience in your city is the job.
Importantly: this role is about getting the right people to act (sign up, show up, apply, move through the talent pipeline, and so on), not about follower or like counts per se.
The tone will differ per city. In The Hague, being able to communicate in Dutch matters a lot, in Delft not so much. You should know your city best, though.
firstMonths: Set up the chapter's LinkedIn and Instagram, plus its WhatsApp or Discord announcements, within SAIN's brand kit.
Announce the chapter, and promote its first events and its first course.
Set up a simple monthly content calendar with the Events and Education Leads.
By June: a chapter community of hundreds of people in your city who follow along, sign up and show up.
responsibilities: Run the chapter's Instagram and LinkedIn, and its WhatsApp and Discord announcements, in line with SAIN's brand kit.
Plan the content calendar each month, in line with SAIN's content pillars and the chapter's goals.
Promote events and courses: build anticipation, drive sign-ups, and post recaps afterwards.
Reshare relevant content from SAIN, our advisors and partner organisations.
Keep the chapter's page on the SAIN website up to date.
Sync with the other chapters' Communications Leads at least once a quarter.
Attend to the chapter's communications inbox, and escalate matters to your Director or SAIN's national team where appropriate.
goodFitIf: Have run social media, a newsletter, a blog or a student magazine, or have done content creation or journalism.
Write clearly and have a good visual sense (Canva, Figma or similar).
Care about consistency: the right tone and the right logo, every time.
Have a genuine interest in AI safety.
alsoStrong: A background in communications, marketing, design or journalism.
Experience growing an audience from zero.
Fluent Dutch (especially valuable in The Hague).

logistics.compensation: €34–42k a year at full-time (40 hours), pro-rated to your hours.

apply.heading: One form, and a decision by mid-December.
apply.intro: Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, with priority to early applicants. The soft deadline is {date}.

form.label: Application form
form.detail: Your CV, a few short written questions, and one question for each role you apply for. About 45 minutes.

workSample.label: Work sample
workSample.detail: If your application stands out, we'll give you a short task that mirrors the role you'll be doing, which takes about two hours.

interview.label: Interview
interview.detail: 45 minutes with two people from SAIN, including a discussion of your work sample.

decision.label: Decision
decision.detail: By mid-December we invite a starting team of four people per city.

start.label: Start
start.detail: If you are in the starting team, your work will really kick off in mid-January!

hearBack.heading: Everyone who applies hears back from us.
hearBack.body: If you are not in the starting team, you are still the start of the chapter’s community! We will send you what you need to join SAIN’s online community, so you are among the first to hear about new activities and opportunities in your city.

strongEnough.heading: We only start a chapter when the team is strong enough.
strongEnough.body: If we do not have strong enough applications to start the incubation in a particular city, we will open a second round later on.

about.heading: About SAIN
about.body: Safe AI Netherlands (SAIN) is a Dutch non-profit developing the talent the Netherlands needs to address the risks of transformative AI. We build the national AI safety talent pipeline to get people from first contact to first real contribution. Then we connect them to the institutions and organisations that need them.
about.visa: We do not sponsor visas. If you are in the Netherlands on a student residence permit, you can still apply.

close.heading: Three new chapters. Twelve people to start them.
close.body: Apply by {date}. We read applications every week, so applying early means hearing back early.
